title: Private Deployment Request Fast-Lane and Risk Scoring Rubric for Network-Restricted Customers
creator: Avery Chen
description: Problem: We are receiving an increasing volume of Private/VPC/on-prem request tickets from enterprise customers that include complex networking constraints (air-gapped, strict egress rules, legacy firewall devices) and non-uniform upgrade requirements. Current hand-triage is slow, inconsistent, and hard to explain to customers. Goal: Design a reproducible, auditable intake + risk-scoring rubric and a 'Fast-Lane' routing path for low-risk, high-value customers that can accelerate time-to-onboarding while preserving safety and operational guardrails. Deliverables: 1) a documented scoring rubric with clear thresholds and examples; 2) an intake form schema for Solutions Engineering and Sales to capture required signals; 3) automation hooks to map score -> lane (Fast / Standard / Remediation); 4) playbook pages (internal for Eng/SE/Support) and customer-facing expectations for each lane; 5) a small pilot with 6 real incoming requests to validate accuracy and SLAs.
acceptance_criteria: Scoring rubric published in Confluence with worked examples for 8 common network scenarios
Intake form (Google Form + API mapping) that captures all rubric signals and produces a numeric score
Automation mapping created in the intake flow that assigns lane labels (fast / standard / remediation) and notifies the correct triage queue
PS/SE and Sales trained on the new expectations; pilot run completed with at least 6 customer requests and feedback captured
Operational metrics to track: time-to-first-response, time-to-scope, % routed to Fast-Lane; baseline captured before rollout
steps: Workshop w/ Solutions Eng, Support, Security (2026-03-11): finalize rubric factors and weights
Draft intake form fields and backend mapping (2026-03-12)
Build simple scoring lambda + Slack routing prototype (Eng spike, 2d)
Run pilot with SE-owned requests and collect feedback (2026-03-18 to 2026-03-26)
Iterate rubric and update playbook; prepare handoff for wider rollout and automation in Zendesk/GQL intake (by 2026-04-01)
notes: Design trade-offs: prefer conservative defaults for customers with active compliance requirements (treat as higher risk even if networking looks simple).
Opportunity: map scoring to our revenue tiers to prioritize high-value customers into Fast-Lane while maintaining fairness for self-serve where applicable.
Risk: mis-scoring could escalate operational load; include manual override and forced review flags for ambiguous cases.
Related: this rubric will later feed into Dedicated capacity gating and scheduled upgrade windows for private installs.
comments: 2026-03-11 Avery Chen: Ran kickoff with SE/Support/Security. Agreed rubric factors: network openness (egress/ingress), upgrade cadence constraints, customer SLA/RPO needs, KMS/HSM complexity, third-party proxy/firewall devices. Action: Engineering to validate feasibility of quick scoring lambda.

2026-03-12 Marco Alvarez: Feasibility review done. Engineering suggests capturing firewall vendor + NAT topology fields to estimate effort. Proposed a temporary Fast-Lane SLA: 48h time-to-scope for scored < 20. Adding an explicit 'requires security review' flag if KMS/HSM present.
2026-03-12 Leah Patel (Security): Security will accept automated routing for low-risk scores (<15) but requires manual check for any item with 'airgap' or 'HSM'. Will document exceptions list.

2026-03-13 Nina Park (Solutions Eng): Drafted intake form and included optional network diagrams, VPN configs, and patch window expectations. Suggested a checkbox 'customer able to run connectivity probe' to expedite assessment.
2026-03-13 Marco Alvarez: Added automation TODOs for Slack channel routing and Zendesk tag mapping. Created pilot cohort of 6 inbound requests (SE owners assigned).
decisions: Adopt a numeric 0-100 scoring scale. Thresholds: Fast-Lane <=20, Standard 21-50, Remediation >50.
Fast-Lane SLA: 48h time-to-first-scope; Standard SLA: 5 business days; Remediation: case-by-case with security/eng triage.
Manual override allowed for SE/Support leads with justification logged in ticket.
